column1: Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Have a baking sheet and a 9x13-inch baking dish ready and line a plate with paper towels.
Pound each chicken breast under parchment to an even 1/2-inch thickness, then season both sides with salt and pepper.
Prepare three shallow dishes: flour with 1/4 tsp salt; eggs whisked with milk; breadcrumbs mixed with half the Parmesan, 1/2 tsp pepper, and 1/4 tsp salt.
Coat each breast in flour, dip in the egg mixture, then press into the breadcrumb mixture and set on the baking sheet.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Fry the chicken in batches until golden and crisp, 3–4 minutes per side, then drain on the paper towels.
Spread 2 1/2 cups marinara in the baking dish and lay the chicken on top. Add about 1 tbsp sauce to each piece, then some basil, the remaining Parmesan, and a slice of provolone.
Bake uncovered 15–20 minutes until the cheese is melted and browned and the chicken is cooked through.
